title: Maximum Sum on a Circle

concept.title: A circular block is a block, or the rest minus a block
body: On a circle a block of consecutive elements either fits in the array as usual, or it **wraps around** the end. A wrapping block is everything *except* a normal block in the middle. So its sum is `total - (sum of that middle block)`, and it is the largest when the middle block has the **smallest** possible sum.

Both the maximum and the minimum block sums come from one Kadane pass each. There is one special case: if all numbers are negative, the "wrapping" block would be empty, which is not allowed; then the answer is just the largest single element (which is the ordinary Kadane result).

statement: The `n` numbers are written on a circle, so the last number is followed by the first one. Find the largest sum of a non-empty block of consecutive numbers on the circle. A block may use each number at most once.

examples.note: The block 6, 5, -3, 5 wraps around the end of the array: its sum is 13.

hints: Case 1: the best block does not wrap; use Kadane.
Case 2: the best block wraps; it is the total minus the smallest block sum in the middle.
If all numbers are negative, return the plain Kadane answer.

explanation: The best wrapping block is the whole circle minus the worst ordinary block. Take the larger of the two cases; an all-negative array is handled separately.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

total = sum(a)
curMax = bestMax = a[0]
curMin = bestMin = a[0]
for i in range(1, n):
    curMax = max(a[i], curMax + a[i])
    bestMax = max(bestMax, curMax)
    curMin = min(a[i], curMin + a[i])
    bestMin = min(bestMin, curMin)
print(bestMax if bestMax < 0 else max(bestMax, total - bestMin))
